old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a desk setup, focusing on a glass filled with water and a green pencil partially submerged in it. The pencil is labeled "Faber-Castell" and appears to have "9000" printed on it. To the left of the glass, there is a small bottle with a yellow cap, with a label that includes the word "Aceite" partially visible. In the background, part of a computer keyboard is visible, suggesting an office or study environment. The lighting is consistent throughout the video, indicating it was shot indoors under artificial light. The scene remains static with no camera movement or other action occurring.

caption: The video captures a clear drinking glass on a desk holding two liquid layers—a transparent lower portion and a yellow upper band—through which a green Faber-Castell 9000 pencil leans at a tilt. A small bottle with a yellow cap sits to the left, a black monitor and keyboard fill the background, and a tall clear bottle with a green label edges in at the far left. Throughout the excerpt the viewpoint drifts, translating the glass, pencil, capped bottle and background rightward while the leftmost bottle grows from a thin sliver toward a fuller view. The liquid layers stay level and undisturbed, with no pouring, stirring or rising bubbles. The pencil keeps the same angle relative to the glass, its apparent kink at the yellow–clear boundary being a constant refraction artifact rather than a real bend. A small bluish reflection near the top rim shifts in step with the drifting camera.
